name: Founding of the Cistercian Order
summary: Robert of Molesme founded a new monastery at Cîteaux in Burgundy in 1098, seeking to follow the Rule of St. Benedict literally and avoid the wealth of Cluny. The order transformed when Bernard of Clairvaux joined in 1113, bringing charismatic leadership and austere spirituality. By 1200 the Cistercians had over 500 abbeys across Europe, clearing forests, draining marshes, and revolutionizing European agriculture. Their churches, stripped of ornamentation, defined Romanesque austerity.
outcomes: Cîteaux Abbey founded by Robert of Molesme
Bernard of Clairvaux joins 1113; transforms the order
Agricultural and architectural achievements across Europe

_quarry.structural_significance: One of the great institutional innovations of the 12th century; the Cistercian network of abbeys was the most effective agricultural enterprise of medieval Europe.
